chain.label: Captain untrained in manual weight and balance computation
chain.trigger: the captain was not trained to manually compute an airplane's weight and balance because he had attended the company's reduced training course

chain.label: Departed MEM with weight and balance calculations unresolved, planning to finish them in flight
chain.trigger: he did not leave a copy of the load manifest at MEM before the accident flight departed because he had to manually calculate the airplane's weight and balance, and the calculations were not completed before takeoff

caused_by.evidence: Air Tahoma's handheld company computer was not working before the flight departed... the captain was not trained to manually compute an airplane's weight and balance

chain.label: No written crossfeed restrictions; prior employer left shutoff valve closure to captain's discretion; unfounded pilot belief that shutoff valves fail
chain.trigger: a Safety Board review of Air Tahoma's operations and training manuals revealed that the company had no written documentation regarding fuel crossfeed operations restrictions

chain.label: Captain began in-flight crossfeed but intentionally left the right fuel tank shutoff valve open, contrary to the QRH, AFM and placard
chain.trigger: the captain added that he intentionally kept the valve open because he thought that Convair fuel tank shutoff valves tended to fail after being shut off

caused_by.evidence: Nolinor Aviation's FOM stated that the fuel tank valve on the tank to be shut off should be closed, 'subject to the captain's discretion'

chain.label: Captain preoccupied with weight and balance recalculation; neither pilot monitored the crossfeed or the fuel quantity gauges
chain.trigger: the captain was preoccupied with the weight and balance calculations during critical portions of the flight and, as a result, he did not monitor the fuel crossfeed operations

caused_by.evidence: he decided to take off and finish the weight and balance paperwork during the flight... because he used the incorrect fuel burn moment value, the calculations were not computing correctly, and the captain became preoccupied with trying to identify the mistake

chain.label: Unused left-tank fuel transferred through the open crossfeed and right shutoff valves into the right tank, producing a growing lateral fuel imbalance
chain.trigger: all of the fuel from the airplane's left tank that was not used by the engines transferred into the right tank because the captain intentionally kept the right fuel tank shutoff valve open

caused_by.evidence: the fuel not consumed by the right engine was allowed to flow back through the right fuel boost pump and into the right fuel tank
he did not monitor the fuel crossfeed operations, which resulted in a fuel imbalance and unusual airplane handling characteristics

chain.label: Captain ignored the first officer's five repeated reports of heavy, uncommanded control forces and initiated no troubleshooting
chain.trigger: The captain did not respond to the first officer's first five comments regarding the airplane's unusual handling characteristics, which occurred over a period of less than 6 minutes

caused_by.evidence: the first officer stated that the control wheel felt 'funny.' He added, 'feels like I need a lot of force. it is pushing to the right for some reason'

chain.label: In-range checklist, which includes the fuel panel check, started about 14 minutes late at 3,000 feet
chain.trigger: the captain should have started the in-range checklist about 14 minutes earlier (shortly before 0035; at which time, the airplane was at an altitude of about 12,000 feet)

caused_by.evidence: the captain was preoccupied with the weight and balance calculations during critical portions of the flight

chain.label: On finally recognizing the crossfeed was still open, captain took no corrective action and did not turn on the right fuel boost pump
chain.trigger: The captain responded, 'I got the crossfeed open. just keep power on.'

caused_by.evidence: While performing the in-range checklist, the captain stated that they had an 'imbalance on this...crossfeed I left open.'

chain.label: Left tank, which was feeding both engines, exhausted while about 5,600 lbs of fuel sat isolated in the right tank
chain.trigger: the fuel in the left fuel tank, which was providing fuel to both engines, was exhausted

caused_by.evidence: all of the fuel from the left fuel tank not used by the engines could transfer into the right fuel tank in a relatively short period of time
the crew missed several opportunities to identify the ongoing fuel crossfeed operations and determine that the airplane's fuel was imbalanced

chain.label: Dual engine flameout on short final as air, not fuel, was drawn into both engine-driven fuel pumps
chain.trigger: both engine-driven fuel pumps drew air from the left tank into the fuel system instead of fuel from the right tank, resulting in a dual-engine flameout

caused_by.evidence: when the left fuel tank was exhausted of fuel, the left fuel boost pump most likely continued to operate, which allowed air to enter the fuel system and reduced the fuel pressure to the left and right engine-driven fuel pump inlets

If the captain had turned on the right fuel boost pump after he identified that he had left the crossfeed valve switch open, it is possible that the right engine would have received sufficient fuel pressure to continue to operate; however, there is no evidence that he did so

chain.label: Power loss occurred at about 2,400 feet on short final, leaving no altitude or time for a restart
chain.trigger: the pilots most likely would not have had sufficient time or altitude to restart the engines because they lost power during short final approach

chain.label: Airplane struck trees and terrain 1.2 miles short of runway 36R and was destroyed
chain.trigger: The airplane initially impacted the top of a stand of trees... about 1.2 miles short of the approach end of runway 36R

caused_by.evidence: the first officer stated, 'we've lost both of them'... The wreckage was located about 1.2 miles short of runway 36R
they lost power during short final approach

chain.label: First officer killed; captain received minor injuries
chain.trigger: The first officer was killed, and the captain received minor injuries

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for the first officer was 'massive acute body trauma'... The airplane was destroyed by impact forces
